blme_kernel: l0_per_token = (feature_acts > 0).float().sum(dim=-1); mean_active_features_l0 = mean_over_samples(l0_per_token.mean()); max_active_features_l0 = max_over_samples(l0_per_token.max()); sae_total_dict_size = sae.cfg.d_sae  (sae_features.py:149-167)
metric_definition: SAE feature-usage stats. L0 = mean number of strictly-active (>0) SAE features per token; density = per-feature fraction of tokens active; dead-fraction = features never active across all tokens. BLME's task outputs mean/max L0 + dict size only.
reference_primary_class: sae_lens.SAE.from_pretrained(release, sae_id).encode(acts) -> StandardSAE (jbloom/GPT2-Small-SAEs-Reformatted, Joseph Bloom gpt2-small-res-jb release; the canonical Anthropic/Bricken-style residual-stream SAE served through SAELens).
tolerance_note: The BLME L0 kernel and the numpy reference operate on the IDENTICAL SAELens-encoded feature matrix. The per-token L0 counts are EXACT integers (bit-identical between torch and numpy), and the reference mean is computed in BLME's own float32 dtype, so the kernel stats agree to 0.0. (A float64 higher-precision mean differs by ~5e-5 due purely to float32 accumulation over ~2700-active-feature rows — this is BLME's own dtype choice, not a kernel divergence; reported as 'full_matrix_f64_info_diff'.) The trained-SAE pipeline itself is FAITHFUL: SAELens's own SAE.encode produced the features.
verdict: PARITY (stat kernels) + FAITHFUL (trained-SAE pipeline). BLME's L0 kernel == independent numpy reference to 0.0 (float32 dtype) on SAELens-encoded features from the real pretrained gpt2-small-res-jb SAE; per-token counts are bit-exact integers.
